route.meaning: Selectively move the current DomainSpec v2 Product lineage into one self-contained Craft root while retaining all unselected old-name paths as immutable migration and historical evidence.

development_inventory_policy.migration_rule: a directory migrates only when a later phase names its exact dependency closure

phases.action: Refresh the source manifest, path-consumer inventory, git-state capture, and map digests against one frozen current working-source epoch.
phases.completion: Every selected input has an exact path, digest, git state, owner, and migration disposition; no source byte changes during the capture.

phases.action: Materialize the selected active-backend canonical definition closure under cyberAlchemy-v2/craft/authority/definitions, converting YAML authorities and criterion records to deterministic JSON while preserving stable IDs, three definition voices, provenance, and lifecycle boundaries.
phases.completion: The 13 active backend meta types, 13 JSON criterion records, scoped 17-signature DS-D8 authority, supported backend profile registry, domainspec-v2-D31..D35 state vocabulary, synchronized index, drift audit, schemas, validator, and immutable snapshot manifest close without YAML runtime dependencies or authority inflation.

phases.action: Validate two-run deterministic JSON conversion, exact source-to-output semantic equivalence, reference closure, three-voice completeness, and selected-source digest currentness; then bind one exact owner-reviewed Definition Snapshot candidate.
phases.completion: One immutable Definition Snapshot digest is accepted for later Craft layers; validation alone does not activate ontology, architecture, or implementation.

phases.action: Complete Craft Product, Project, and Method entry surfaces inside cyberAlchemy-v2/craft and bind them to the accepted Definition Snapshot without treating DomainSpec v2 as a predecessor Product.
phases.completion: The self-contained Craft root, Product, Project, Method, and source maps agree on CA2-PRODUCT-CRAFT, CA2-PROJECT-CRAFT, CAV2-D20, same-product-renamed, and the exact Definition Snapshot.

phases.action: Select and migrate only the Product Capability and business-ontology records required by the first meta-type instantiation vertical, binding every record to the accepted Definition Snapshot.
phases.completion: The selected capability and ontology closure is internally complete; unselected product and ontology material remains in legacy roots.

phases.action: Migrate the selected DomainSpec authored source, deterministic compiled graph, and system ontology needed by the first vertical under cyberAlchemy-v2/craft.
phases.completion: The selected D65 definition-to-system-ontology chain is source-bound and deterministic; no ambient ontology runtime output grants admission.

phases.action: Selectively migrate the architecture properties, language-neutral realization contracts, and TypeScript, Python, and Rust bindings required by the first vertical.
phases.completion: Every selected realization closes against the accepted system ontology and retains its exact language/profile identity; unrelated architecture research and development packages remain legacy evidence.

phases.action: Materialize one dependency-closed Node 26 implementation and CLI under cyberAlchemy-v2/craft/implementation, with only the generators, profiles, ports, schemas, tests, fixtures, and conformance providers selected by the first vertical.
phases.completion: The selected Craft implementation installs, typechecks, tests, and builds standalone without borrowing the legacy parent workspace or unselected development directories.

phases.action: Rewrite only consumers in the selected vertical to final Craft paths and retain every unselected old-root occurrence in place as legacy evidence.
phases.completion: Every selected consumer resolves to cyberAlchemy-v2/craft; no global 1,027-file rewrite or evidence relocation is implied.

phases.action: Run the final-path Node 26, generation, three-profile, Operation, Workflow, target-project, independent-conformance, and two-run determinism checks for the selected vertical, then freeze its exact graph.
phases.completion: One selected source-to-target-project-to-independent-conformance vertical passes twice and becomes the first frozen Craft baseline; all unselected legacy roots remain readable and unchanged.

validation_obligations: the canonical active root is cyberAlchemy-v2/craft and every concern root is nested beneath it
M01 migrates definitions before Product Capability, ontology, architecture, realization, or implementation
the Definition Snapshot carries exactly 13 active backend meta types, 13 JSON criterion records, and a scoped 17-signature DS-D8 authority
all Craft definition machine records and criterion schemas are JSON and no destination YAML dependency remains
the 53-directory map remains discovery and preservation evidence rather than a bulk-copy schedule
only exact dependency-closed files and consumers selected by a phase migrate; all others remain legacy evidence
active imports and package identities use Craft roots and names
the final implementation is standalone under the repository Node 26 container
TypeScript, Python, and Rust profile realizations remain selected and independently conformant

Operation and Workflow constraints include declared reads, writes, effects, guards, atomic state and outbox, explicit failure continuation, undeclared-effect rejection, relationship rules, and durable recovery bindings
a mock target project can be created from typed intent and independently checked against exact selected realization and byte digests
two identical runs produce identical target bytes, manifests, and conformance results
no numbered baseline candidate is used as a substitute for final-path validation

execution_blockers.meaning: The latest numbered baseline-v11 candidate has no passing aggregate receipt and is diagnostic evidence only, not a migration source.
The selected active-backend JSON Definition Snapshot does not yet exist under cyberAlchemy-v2/craft/authority/definitions.

claim_ceiling: Revision 2 corrects migration structure and sequence only. It does not itself materialize definitions, copy development directories, rebind consumers, admit a Definition Snapshot, activate ontology or implementation, delete legacy roots, publish, release, deploy, or prove production readiness.
